 Image source, Getty Images Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler speaking to TNT Sports: "These games in the Conference League are different. You have to beat a low block. You have to understand what the opponents are looking for in the game. Therefore, you have to always be patient in these games and I think we did it today. 
 "We didn't play our best game, to be fair. We had a few moments where we were quite lazy with the easy things. We didn't do the simple things on the highest level but in the end we kept a clean sheet, third clean sheet in a row in this tournament and we scored a goal and I think we deserved to win this game."
 On the plan with Pascal Gross after playing 16 games in a row: "At one point we need to manage him as well, but at the moment he just keeps running. He seems to be in a good shape. Today he didn't play the full 90 minutes, also manage the energy from the players like this."
 On Brighton fans getting excited about winning the competition: "They should dream, that's what I always say. We focus on work. We focus on the things we can control. They should dream and hopefully at one point we can fulfil their dream."

 By Sam Drury BBC Sport journalist Sunderland were jeered by the Stadium of Light crowd as their worrying form continued with defeat by Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League. 
 With the Black Cats struggling at the bottom of the Premier League, a first European loss of the campaign will only increase the pressure on head coach Regis le Bris.
 Luka Stojkovic volleyed Dinamo in front in the 22nd minute and there were loud boos from the home fans when in-form striker Dion Beljo doubled the lead 17 minutes later, neatly lifting the ball past Robin Roefs.
 The Sunderland supporters voiced their displeasure again at half-time.
 Le Bris made a quadruple substitution for the start of the second half, leading to a much-improved performance, but there was no way back for the hosts and more booing rang out at full-time.
 Despite the loss on Thursday, their two wins to start the competition mean Sunderland are still reasonably well placed to advance. Like Dinamo, they sit outside the top eight on goal difference halfway through the league phase.
 More concerning is their Premier League form, with their only win coming back in August. This latest setback makes Sunday's home game against Chelsea all the more significant, particularly for Le Bris.
 More to follow. 
 Why is it going so wrong for Le Bris at Sunderland?
